items.html:
Treat the stored (A,T,D,\widehat Y) as exact values, with every (d_i\ne0). Define [ B=D^{-1}AD,\quad C=D^{-1}T,\quad \widehat X=\operatorname{fl}(D\widehat Y),\quad R=T-A\widehat X. ] For (X_=A^{-1}T), the exact identities are [ E:=X_-\widehat X=A^{-1}R,\qquad D^{-1}E=B^{-1}D^{-1}R. ]

If a verified bound (\beta\le\sigma_{\min}(B)), (\beta>0), is available, then [ \boxed{|D^{-1}E|\le\frac{|D^{-1}R|}{\beta}},\qquad \boxed{|E|\le\frac{d_{\max}|D^{-1}R|}{\beta} \le\frac{d_{\max}}{d_{\min}}\frac{|R|}{\beta}}. ] Here (|\cdot|) may be the vector 2-norm, or spectral/Frobenius norm for multiple right-hand sides; (d_{\max/\min}=\max/\min_i|d_i|). Retaining the weighted residual gives the tighter bound. Eigenvalue magnitudes alone cannot replace singular values for a nonnormal (B).

For rounded (\widehat B=B+\Delta B), (\widehat C=C+\Delta C), put [ r_s=\widehat C-\widehat B\widehat Y,\qquad \delta X=\widehat X-D\widehat Y. ] Then [ \boxed{D^{-1}R =r_s-\Delta C+\Delta B\widehat Y-BD^{-1}\delta X}. ] Thus the residual of the rounded scaled system alone leaves a gap. Computing the residual from the original encoded (A,T,\widehat X) includes all these effects automatically.

The stability denominator still needs correction: if the certificate concerns (\widehat B), use [ \beta=\widehat\beta-\varepsilon_B>0,\qquad \widehat\beta\le\sigma_{\min}(\widehat B),\quad \varepsilon_B\ge|\widehat B-B|_2. ] Rounding when selecting (D) causes no separate error: define the transformation using the actual stored (D).

High precision alone is not a rigorous enclosure. Certify (\rho\ge|D^{-1}(T-A\widehat X)|), including residual/scaling evaluation errors; then (\delta=d_{\max}\rho/\beta) bounds absolute error. If (\delta<|\widehat X|), [ \frac{|E|}{|X_*|} \le\frac{\delta}{|\widehat X|-\delta}. ]

Tiny test: use (A=\begin{pmatrix}2&1\1&3\end{pmatrix}), (D=\operatorname{diag}(3,7)), (T=(1,1)^T). Solve the rounded scaled system, round (D\widehat Y), then use exact rational representations of the stored floats to check both boxed residual identities and the forward bound against (X_*=(2/5,1/5)^T). Nonbinary scaling ratios exercise the roundoff gap.
